question: Flipping a coin 10 times and getting heads every time
explanation: Each flip is 1/2, so 1/2 × 1/2 … ten times = 1/1,024.

question: Being dealt a royal flush in a 5-card poker hand
explanation: There are 4 royal flushes (one per suit) out of 2,598,960 possible 5-card hands.

question: Rolling two dice and getting a total of 7
explanation: 6 of the 36 combinations add up to 7 (1+6, 2+5, 3+4, and the reverse). It's the most common total.

question: Winning the Powerball jackpot with one ticket
explanation: You need the 5 white balls out of 69 (11,238,513 combinations) and the red ball out of 26: 11,238,513 × 26 = 292,201,338.

question: At least two people sharing a birthday in a group of 23
explanation: Surprisingly about 50.7%! With 23 people there are 253 possible pairs, so a match is more likely than not. (ignoring leap years)

question: Rolling a Yahtzee (five of a kind) in a single roll of 5 dice
explanation: The first die can be anything, the 4 others must match it: (1/6)^4 = 1/1,296.

question: Guessing a random 4-digit PIN on the first try
explanation: There are 10,000 possible codes from 0000 to 9999.

question: Being dealt pocket aces in Texas Hold'em
explanation: 6 ways to get two aces out of 1,326 possible starting hands: 1 in 221.

question: Hitting your number on a single spin of European roulette
explanation: 37 pockets (1 to 36 + the zero), only one is yours. The payout is 35 to 1, that's where the casino makes money.

question: Shuffling a playlist of 10 songs and getting them back in the original order
explanation: 10 songs can be ordered in 10! = 3,628,800 ways.

question: Your random Secret Santa draw (4 people) working out with nobody drawing themselves
explanation: Out of the 24 ways to hand out the names, 9 have nobody getting themselves. So it fails more often than it works!

question: Being dealt four of a kind in a 5-card poker hand
explanation: 13 ranks × 48 choices for the 5th card = 624 hands out of 2,598,960.

question: Rolling three sixes with three dice
Winning the EuroMillions jackpot with one ticket
explanation: 5 numbers out of 50 (2,118,760 combinations) times 2 stars out of 12 (66 combinations) = 139,838,160.

question: Beating a random opponent 5 times in a row at rock paper scissors
explanation: Each game you have 1 chance in 3 to win (ties count as fails here): (1/3)^5 = 1/243.

question: Guessing a random number between 1 and 100 on the first try
explanation: Only 1 good answer out of 100.

question: Being dealt a flush (not a straight flush) in a 5-card poker hand
explanation: C(13,5) × 4 suits = 5,148 hands, minus the 40 straight flushes = 5,108 out of 2,598,960.

question: Your birthday being on February 29
explanation: One day every 4 years: 1 day out of 1,461 (365 × 4 + 1). Roughly 5 million people in the world are "leaplings".

question: A shuffled deck having at least one card still in its original position
explanation: About 63.2%, it's 1 - 1/e. Weirdly it's almost the same for 10 cards or 1,000 cards.

question: Getting a blackjack (ace + 10-value card) on the first two cards from one deck
explanation: 4 aces × 16 ten-value cards (10, J, Q, K) = 64 hands out of 1,326.

question: Flipping a coin 20 times and getting heads every time
explanation: (1/2)^20 = 1/1,048,576. Double the flips, and the odds get squared.

question: Rolling at least one 6 in 4 rolls of a die
explanation: 1 - (5/6)^4 = 51.8%. A famous bet from 1654 that started probability theory (Pascal and Fermat).

question: Rolling at least one double six in 24 rolls of two dice
explanation: 1 - (35/36)^24 = 49.1%, just under half. The gambler Chevalier de Méré lost money thinking it was over 50%.

question: Being dealt 13 cards of the same suit in bridge
explanation: 4 perfect hands out of 635,013,559,600 possible bridge hands. People claim it happened way more often than that, usually with a new deck that wasn't shuffled enough.

question: Winning the UK Lotto (6 numbers out of 59)
explanation: C(59,6) = 45,057,474 possible tickets.

question: A monkey typing random letters writing "hello" in 5 keystrokes
explanation: 26 letters for each of the 5 keys: 26^5 = 11,881,376.

question: Rolling 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 in that order with 6 rolls of a die
Rolling each number exactly once in 6 rolls of a die (any order)
explanation: 6! = 720 good orders out of 46,656 possible results.

question: Getting a full house in a 5-card poker hand
Passing a 10-question multiple choice test (4 options) with 7 or more by guessing
explanation: Add the chances of 7, 8, 9 and 10 good answers with 1/4 per question: about 0.35%.

question: Drawing 5 cards and getting only hearts
explanation: C(13,5) = 1,287 all-heart hands out of 2,598,960.

question: A random 5-card poker hand having at least a pair
explanation: 1,302,540 hands have nothing (high card only), a bit more than half. So almost exactly 1 in 2 hands has a pair or better.

question: Two people both picking the same random number between 1 and 10
explanation: Whatever the first person picks, the second has 1 chance in 10 to match.

question: Looking at a 24h clock at a random minute and seeing all 4 digits the same
explanation: Only 00:00, 11:11 and 22:22 work, 3 minutes out of 1,440 in a day.

question: Rolling a Yahtzee within 3 rolls (keeping the dice that match)
explanation: If you always keep the most common number and reroll the rest, you get it about 4.5% of the time.

question: 5 dice all showing different numbers
explanation: 6 × 5 × 4 × 3 × 2 = 720 good results out of 7,776.

question: 3 kids each drawing their own name out of a hat
explanation: 3 names can be drawn in 6 orders, only one gives everyone their own name.

question: Winning the Mega Millions jackpot with one ticket
explanation: 5 numbers out of 70 (12,103,014 combinations) × 1 Mega Ball out of 25 = 302,575,350.

question: Picking the right card out of a full deck twice in a row
explanation: 1/52 each time (card put back): 1/2,704.

question: Two random students in a class of 30 sharing a birthday
explanation: About 70.6%. With 30 people there are 435 possible pairs.

question: Rolling a total of 10 with three dice
explanation: 27 of the 216 combinations give 10. 10 and 11 are the most common totals with 3 dice.

question: A random card from a deck being a face card (J, Q, K)
explanation: 12 face cards out of 52.

question: Being dealt two pair in a 5-card poker hand
Being dealt three of a kind (not a full house) in a 5-card poker hand
Being dealt a straight flush (not royal) in a 5-card poker hand
explanation: 9 straight flushes per suit (5-high to king-high) × 4 suits = 36 hands.

question: Drawing 2 socks from a drawer with 10 black and 10 white and getting a pair
explanation: 45 black pairs + 45 white pairs = 90 good draws out of 190, a bit less than half.

question: Guessing a 3-digit lock code on the first try
explanation: 1,000 combinations from 000 to 999. Trying them all takes less than an hour.

question: Getting exactly 5 heads in 10 coin flips
explanation: 252 ways out of 1,024. Even the most likely result happens less than 1 time in 4.

question: Guessing a random 6-digit 2FA code
explanation: 1,000,000 possible codes, and they change every 30 seconds.

question: Seating 5 friends at random and they end up in alphabetical order
explanation: 5! = 120 possible orders.

question: Winning on red 5 times in a row at European roulette
explanation: 18 red pockets out of 37 each spin: (18/37)^5, about 2.7%.

question: No two people sharing a birthday in a group of 70
explanation: Only about 0.08%. With 70 people a shared birthday is almost certain (99.9%).

question: Guessing an 8-letter password made of random lowercase letters on the first try
explanation: 26^8 = 208,827,064,576. Sounds safe, but a computer can try that many in a few hours.

question: Getting a 6 on a single roll of a die
explanation: The classic. 1 face out of 6.

question: Getting a sum of 2 or 12 with two dice
explanation: Only double 1 or double 6: 2 combinations out of 36.

question: 5 random people all born on different days of the week
Picking the winner of an 8-horse race completely at random
explanation: 1 horse out of 8 (if they were all equally good, which they're not).

question: Typing 3 random letters and spelling "CAT"
explanation: 26^3 = 17,576 possible 3-letter combinations.

question: Your phone number ending with 4 identical digits (0000, 1111…)
explanation: 10 good endings out of 10,000.

question: Shuffled deck: the top two cards are both aces
explanation: 4/52 × 3/51 = 12/2,652 = 1/221. Same odds as pocket aces.
